newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan says Delhi crash plane cargo charter.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan says Delhi crash plane cargo charter.

text.p: The Kazakh Airlines plane which collided in mid-air with a Saudi Boeing 747 near Delhi on Tuesday was a chartered Ilyushin Il-76 cargo aircraft carrying 38 passengers and crew, including one child, Kazakh transport officials said.
Initial reports from India had identified the plane, on which all on board were feared killed, as a Tupolev Tu-154.

The plane, chartered by a firm in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek, took off from Chimkent in southern Kazakhstan for the Indian capital, a Kazakh Transport Ministry spokesman told Reuters. Many of the 28 passengers were Kyrgyz nationals.
Kaud Bayturiev, deputy airport director in the Kazakh capital Almaty, told Reuters there was a crew of 10 on board the plane, which had the registration number 76435.
He could not say what cargo it was carrying. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
